review_note: review_required: a Métis family of an Ottawa mother, depicted through the French household they lodged in; dress and looks are reconstructed and say so.

present_on_scene_date.note: Dead or gone before 14 August 1812; in the town on the earlier dates their cards give.

not_in_this_household.note: Everyone the T-3463..T-3467 day readings put in this household is on the card (liberty L-1812-town-days-3463).

persons.name: Jean Baptiste Mirandeau (the elder)

age_band.note: Not recorded; father of Victoire (born 1800 or 1801, Andreas) and older children; drawn at about forty-five.

present_on_scene_date.note: Back at Milwaukee before the evacuation (Porthier). No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: A Frenchman who did blacksmith work at the fort in 1811 and lodged his family at Ouilmette's. On the night of 17 June 1812 he took John Kinzie to Milwaukee; the family were gone before the fort burned. In the town from 1811-05-01 to 1812-06-17: Porthier (Andreas p. 105): her father worked at the fort "the year before" it burned, i.e. 1811, and took Kinzie to Milwaukee on the night of 17 June 1812; "We were not there when the fort was burned". Andreas calls him "a sojourner in Chicago in 1811". Both dates are ours within that.

persons.name: Victoire Mirandeau

age_band.note: Born 1800 or 1801 by collateral evidence (Andreas): 11 or 12 in June 1812.

present_on_scene_date.note: Not at Chicago on 14 August: "we had gone back to Milwaukee" (Andreas p. 105). No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: A daughter of Jean Baptiste Mirandeau and his Ottawa wife; she and her sister Madeline saw the fight between John Kinzie and Lalime (Andreas p. 105). Victoire later lived with the Kinzies as their servant (Andreas p. 105). In the town from 1811-06-01 to 1812-06-18: Victoire: her father worked at the fort "the year before" the burning and the family came down while he was there; they had gone back to Milwaukee before August. The month they came is not recorded (June 1811 is a stand-in). Last attested at sunset on 17 June 1812; their father took the wounded Kinzie to Milwaukee that night, and the family is ended the next day, which is ours.

evidence.quote: My sister Madaline (afterward the wife of John K. Clark) and I saw the fight between old John Kinzie and Lalime

evidence.claim: The fight was at sunset, when the gates were shut.

evidence.quote: In the night he packed up some things, and my father took him to Milwaukee
evidence.claim: That night Victoire's father took the wounded Kinzie to Milwaukee.

evidence.quote: We were not there when the fort was burned—we had gone back to Milwaukee.
evidence.claim: The Mirandeaus were back at Milwaukee before the fort burned.

evidence.quote: He taught us children to speak French, and we all learned to speak Indian of the tribe and mother.
evidence.claim: The Mirandeau children spoke French and their mother's language and had no schooling.

evidence.quote: We had no schools nor education. I never learned to read or write.
